text:
perf-ci-bot: CI perf regression detected on PR #8602 (microbench warmup). Median p50 latency +18% vs baseline. Failing test: tests/perf/microbench_warmup.py::test_warmup_plateau. Full output: https://ci.internal/redwood/8602/results :eyes:

maya: saw the alert. anyone able to repro locally?

ranjit: I pulled the CI artifact and ran a quick local microbench. Repro is noisy but visible. Suspect recent kernel-autoselect heuristic change (PR 8591) — it added more aggressive fallback to quantized kernels when KV hitrate low. :thinking:

olivia: can confirm PR 8591 changed kernel_selector.py to reduce the hysteresis window from 5->1 requests. That would make it flip back/forth if warmup kv_hit oscillates during early batches. I added comments in the PR but it got merged in the release window.

ethan: here's my reproduce command and raw numbers:

```bash
# run from infra/perf
./run_microbench --model=gpt-small --seq=512 --batch=1 --iters=500 --warmup=50
```

Sample output (excerpt):

```
RUN 8602: p50=12.6ms p95=28.1ms tokens/s=124.3
BASE : p50=10.7ms p95=24.9ms tokens/s=145.7
DELTA: p50 +17.8% p95 +12.9% tokens/s -14.8%
Decision: kernel_switch_count=23, kv_cache_hit=0.26 -> fluctuating
```

maya: that kernel_switch_count looks high. normal ~1-2 during warmup.

ranjit: agree. hypothesis: small randomness in early requests drops kv_hit below threshold, triggers fallback to quantized kernel (faster per-op cost but worse throughput here due to different memory layout), then when hit rises it flips back — thrashing. The microbench uses short-lived contexts so it amplifies.

olivia: simple mitigation would be to increase hysteresis to 8 requests or require sustained kv_hit<0.2 for two consecutive windows. I can open a small patch.

ethan: for CI immediate unblock we can either revert the heuristic change in 8591 or bump the microbench threshold temporarily. Reverting is safer for correctness.

maya: can someone open a hotfix PR? We should also mark the release as blocked until we either revert or land a mitigation. This is a rollout blocker for the runtime release.

ranjit: I'll open a rollback PR that restores the old hysteresis and include a test that simulates kv_hit oscillation. assigning to @olivia to follow up with a refined patch.

olivia: on it. I'll also update kernel_selector unit tests to include the microbench reproducer scenario and add an integration perf test to avoid regressions like this.

perf-ci-bot: Noted. CI job for PR 8605 (rollback) queued. If rollback lands, rerun microbench suite and notify this thread. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks team — please post PR links here and ping if you need a backfill of historical perf traces.
